agent_notes: API compatibility: changing `post(url: string)` to `post(url: string, body?: object)` only adds an optional parameter. All 4 existing callers (model-file.service.ts:61, :74, :87 and server-command.service.ts:26) call post(url) and still compile unchanged. Using `body ?? null` keeps their request byte-for-byte the same as before (null body, no JSON content-type).

Mocks and tests: src/angular/src/app/tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts has no post() method, so nothing changes there. Once config.service starts calling post(url, body), the mock and config.service.spec.ts will need a post stub that records the body.

Type surface: `object` accepts arrays, FormData and Blob as well as plain objects. Angular HttpClient serializes plain objects and arrays as JSON with Content-Type application/json and sends FormData and Blob as-is, so nothing breaks. The planned config-set body is a plain object, and the backend reads it via bottle.request.json, which requires the application/json content-type that HttpClient sets automatically for plain objects.
Interaction with shareReplay(1): each post() call still creates its own observable, so request bodies are not shared or cached across calls. There is no new risk of a stale body being replayed.
Performance: no effect. It is one extra argument and no new requests.
Database and schema: none on the frontend. The backend contract change (GET path parameters to POST JSON) already landed in commits fffa81a and fe0e07d.
Blast radius of the changed line: low. It affects the 4 existing POST call sites (bulk file actions and server restart), which behave exactly as before.

Blast radius of the migration as a whole: settings saves are broken until config.service.ts moves to POST (see finding impact-1). This is the risk of shipping a staged change partway, not a defect in this diff.
Verdict: the diff itself is safe and backward compatible. Do not release until config.service.ts is migrated to post(url, body).
